dedupe_keys.name: assessing the benefits and costs of nature based solutions for climate resilience world bank guideline with 8 case studies

description: This World Bank guideline explains how project developers can assess the benefits and costs of nature-based solutions for climate resilience, from scoping benefits and choosing a decision support framework to valuation and cost-benefit analysis, with tiers of analysis matched to time and budget. It covers nature-based solution families such as mangroves, coral reefs, wetlands, urban green spaces and watershed management, and eight case studies that informed World Bank investment projects, including coral reef restoration in the Seychelles, Haizhu Wetland Park, mangrove change in Jamaica and coastal design alternatives protecting an industrial port, each with tables of data, assumptions, costs, benefits and benefit-cost results. It was produced by World Bank and GFDRR staff in 2023, designed by Felixx Landscape Architects and Planners. The report of 99 pages is available as a free PDF under the Creative Commons Attribution CC BY 3.0 IGO licence. Caveats: values come from the individual case studies and are not a harmonised database. It supports economic appraisal of green-blue infrastructure against grey alternatives for flood, coastal and climate adaptation investment; a related record is the Ecosystem Services Valuation Database.
name: Assessing the Benefits and Costs of Nature-Based Solutions for Climate Resilience (World Bank guideline with 8 case studies)
notes: Reference: World Bank (2023). Assessing the Benefits and Costs of Nature-Based Solutions for Climate Resilience: A Guideline for Project Developers. Washington, DC: World Bank. CC BY 3.0 IGO
